stories.headline: Plugin4Shell: zero-click RCE across Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, and Gemini CLI
stories.why_read: AI coding agents' plugin pin can be swapped upstream — keys-to-the-kingdom supply-chain beat.
body: Air Security described Plugin4Shell: an agent can check out a marketplace-pinned plugin commit and still land malicious code, because Git may treat a requested SHA as a branch name. Auto-updating plugins turn that into zero-click remote code execution across Anthropic's Claude Code, OpenAI's Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Google's Gemini CLI.

Anthropic reportedly patched in Claude Code 2.1.179 and OpenAI in Codex 0.146.0; Copilot still lacked a fix in Air's accounting, and Gemini CLI is being retired rather than patched. For anyone living in agent harnesses, update now and treat plugin marketplaces like untrusted CI — Anand's coding-tools shelf in one headline.

stories.headline: Android 17: first since 3.x to ship new APIs without releasing them to AOSP
stories.why_read: HN ~866 pts — GrapheneOS flags a watershed break in Android's open-source contract.
body: GrapheneOS reported that Android 17 is the first release since the 3.x era to add new APIs without publishing them to the Android Open Source Project. Hacker News piled on (~866 points, hundreds of comments) around what that means for OEM forks, privacy builds, and the long-assumed AOSP commons.

Systems story more than phone-review story: if platform surfaces stay proprietary, the open Android that GrapheneOS and others rebuild becomes a second-class citizen. Watch how Google frames the split — and what device makers do next.

stories.headline: Claude Code now reads AGENTS.md when CLAUDE.md is missing
stories.why_read: HN ~666 pts — harness conventions converge; one agents file to rule the desk.
body: Anthropic's Claude Code changelog notes that the tool now reads AGENTS.md if there is no CLAUDE.md. Hacker News celebrated (~666 points): the industry is slowly agreeing that agent instructions belong in a portable, repo-local file instead of a vendor-shaped one.
Practical desk news next to Plugin4Shell on the same fold — standardize the harness file, then harden how plugins land.

stories.headline: US military close call after AI hallucinated an intelligence report
stories.why_read: HN ~461 pts — CNN: false AI intel on a China ship nearly drove a bad call.
body: CNN reported a US military close call after an AI system produced a hallucinated intelligence report involving a Chinese ship. The thread on Hacker News (~461 points) is less dunk and more systems-failure autopsy: verification loops, human review, and what 'AI-assisted intel' actually means under time pressure.
Pairs with yesterday's agent-security wave — when models write the brief, the harness that checks the brief is the product.

stories.headline: How OpenAI used its own LLMs to help design the Jalapeño chip
stories.why_read: IEEE Spectrum on HN — models in the silicon loop, not just the chat loop.
body: IEEE Spectrum's write-up on how OpenAI used its own LLMs while designing its Jalapeño chip landed on Hacker News. The interesting frame is not 'AI replaces chip designers' — it is models as assistants inside EDA-adjacent workflows where the cost of a wrong suggestion is measured in fab spin.
Chips + agents shelf for Anand: inference demand creates silicon; silicon design now borrows the models it will host.

stories.headline: Cactus Needle 3: 8–29MB automation models that claim DeepSeek V4 Flash parity
stories.why_read: Show HN ~200 pts — tiny on-device agents for the LocalLLaMA taste map.
body: Cactus Compute's Needle 3 Show HN pitches automation models in the 8–29MB range that can match DeepSeek V4 Flash on their automation benchmarks. Whether the evals travel, the product thesis is clear: agent loops that fit in edge memory instead of a frontier quota.
Local-inference beat beside Bonsai compression holdovers — intelligence-per-watt still decides who ships offline agents.

stories.headline: Austin Fire Department flags Cybercab: no wheel, no pedals, touchscreen tow?
stories.why_read: Local Austin beat — first responders trained on touchscreen move-outs as Cybercabs roll.
body: The Daily Texan reported Austin Fire Department concerns as Cybercabs entered public service: without a steering wheel or pedals, moving a stuck vehicle in an emergency means touchscreen control after gaining access. Tesla provided multi-day training and guidebooks; AFD had not yet handled a Cybercab emergency as of the piece.

About 49 Cybercabs were registered in Austin in the reporting — a thin fleet next to hundreds of Waymos, with a wider geofence. Hold beside NHTSA's Special Order clock: ops reality on local streets, not just FMVSS paperwork.

stories.headline: Cloudflare: saving another 100TB of RAM — with math
stories.why_read: HN ~375 pts — fleet memory as a first-class product surface.
body: Cloudflare's follow-up on saving another 100TB of RAM via careful data-structure and math work hit Hacker News (~375 points). It is the rare infra post that reads like a performance thriller without a new product launch attached.
Systems craft for anyone running agent sidecars and edge fleets: RAM still has a price tag even when GPUs steal the headlines.

stories.headline: Starship Flight 14 locked to ~Sep 28 — first orbit + 26 Starlink V3 still the goal
stories.why_read: SpaceX slipped from Sep 22; India Today/TeslaNorth confirm Monday NET pending approval.
body: SpaceX is now targeting Starship Flight 14 as early as Monday, September 28, pending regulatory approval — a roughly six-day slip from the prior September 22 window. The public profile still aims at Starship's first orbital attempt (~275 km, about six orbits) with 26 Starlink V3 satellites and Super Heavy recovery offshore in the Gulf.
Keep Construction Physics' Raptor manufacturing essay beside the countdown: cadence and engine learning curves are what turn a spectacular test into a reusable logistics system.

stories.headline: Researchers used Anthropic's Claude to help breach OpenAI — $6,500 bounty
stories.why_read: TechCrunch Sep 18 — rival model in the bug-bounty loop that reached employee Codex/GitHub.
body: Hacktron AI researchers, working through OpenAI's bug-bounty program, used Anthropic's Claude (ultimately Opus-class) while chaining flaws that led to takeover of OpenAI employee ChatGPT/Codex accounts and demonstrated GitHub organization access via a harmless PR. OpenAI paid a $6,500 bounty; researchers say they did not view source.

Yesterday's HN heap-overflow/SSO write-up was the technical spine; today's frame is models-as-offensive-assistants. Update the mental model: agent coding security is both Plugin4Shell and Claude-in-the-red-team.

body: A write-up on Prinz AI claims GPT-6 Astra helped solve a World War I German radio cipher, and Hacker News took the bait. Treat the historiography carefully; treat the workflow seriously — tool use, search, and iterative hypothesis against dusty ciphertext.
Human-interest AI shelf: models as research assistants for archives, not just code factories.

stories.why_read: HN ~280 pts — developmental biology that reframes 'one brain' intuition.

Physics/Chem/Math-adjacent kindness on the pinned taste map — pure curiosity between agent CVEs.

Love/Laughter/Kindness amplifiers include making hard ideas hospitable — Tao's beat lands squarely on Anand's pinned map.

Companion to the 100TB RAM post: Cloudflare is having a systems weekend.
